fatal_errors: The proposed experimental platform does not reconstruct the target DFT–MTP–FEP method, its TaVCrW refractory-alloy system, or its thermodynamic mechanism.

The cited evidence supports neutron imaging of liquid immiscibility and qualitative melting onset, but not synchronized calorimetry/dilatometry/neutron measurements or the claimed ±1% and ±5% precision.

Fast scanning calorimetry at up to 10^3 K/s is not readily compatible with the cited neutron imaging protocol, which acquired radiographs at discrete 20–25 °C intervals in a furnace; no synchronization feasibility is demonstrated.

Neutron imaging can reveal macroscopic phase separation only when sufficient neutron-transmission contrast exists; it does not generally provide liquid-phase thermodynamic functions or quantitative latent heat and volume changes.
Cross-validation against CALPHAD is not decisive when CALPHAD is also used to adjust the measured outputs, creating circular validation and inheriting database uncertainty.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses most requested observables and includes numerical performance claims and a falsification threshold, so its broad problem alignment is reasonable. However, it is scientifically unrelated to the hidden target, which replaces EAM/TI with a high-fidelity MTP/FEP free-energy workflow and tests electronic and short-range-order contributions in BCC TaVCrW. None of the target conditions, mechanisms, benchmark agreements, computational savings, or quantitative melting shifts are recovered. As an alternative approach, the proposal remains inadequately supported: the evidence only establishes qualitative in-situ neutron observation of melting and liquid segregation, while offering no support for calorimetric or volumetric precision, broad applicability across HEA families, or extraction of general liquid thermodynamics. The benchmark test has some discriminating value, but reliance on CALPHAD both for adjustment and validation weakens it substantially.
